posts.title: 0.05 seconds
posts.notes: Check the latest reported 0 to 60 figure for the Roadster before posting. Reports differ, so the copy says "about half a second".
posts.caption:
0.05 seconds.

That is how long it takes to judge a web page. In a well-known study, people rated how appealing a page looked after seeing it for 50 milliseconds, and their snap judgments matched what they said after a longer look (Lindgaard, Fernandes, Dudek and Brown, 2006).

The new Tesla Roadster demo claims 0 to 60 mph in about half a second. That is ten times longer than your visitor needs to make up their mind about your site.

Before the copy, the animation or the clever idea, layout, type, colour and space do the first job. What does yours say in 50 ms?
posts.first_comment: Study: Lindgaard, Fernandes, Dudek and Brown (2006), Behaviour & Information Technology. oopsweb.co

posts.title: World Usability Day: five checks
posts.notes: Post on the day (Thu 12 Nov). The PDF is the swipeable version.
posts.caption:
Happy World Usability Day. Here are five checks you can run on your own site before your coffee gets cold.

1. Tap targets. WCAG 2.2 level AA asks for at least 24 px. Apple suggests 44, Material 48.
2. Contrast. Level AA asks for 4.5 to 1 on normal text.
3. Focus. Tab through your page. Can you see where you are?
4. Line length. 45 to 75 characters a line; typographers aim for about 66.
5. Error messages. Say what went wrong and how to fix it.

Then do the sixth check: watch one real person use it. It tells you more than a week of meetings.

posts.title: Play is a design principle
posts.notes: Children’s Day in India is Sat 14 Nov. The Teeter game page shows the date on its hero, so we used Perigee, which does not.
posts.caption:
Happy Children's Day.

Play is a design principle: a good interface lets you try things before it asks you to read anything.

Perigee is a gravity puzzle we made for the browser. Launch a probe past planets and moons and let their pull carry it to the beacon. Forty hand-made levels across five systems, free to play with a mouse, a trackpad or a finger.
